html:
SMTO-EXE-0242 — The Docker action took too long and was stopped

GUID: 0d2f292f-1ea2-5a14-9209-bb168fc77766
Slug: docker-operation-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The Docker action ran past its time limit, so SMTO stopped waiting for it. Docker may have finished part of the work, or may still be finishing it in the background.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a minute, then ask SMTO in this conversation to show the current state of the containers, images or Compose project involved. Docker can keep working after SMTO stops waiting, so the result may already be there.
  2. If the work is done, you don't need to do anything else. Running it again could start or change something twice.
  3. If it is not done and the job is large, such as a big image download or build, ask SMTO to try again with a time limit of up to five minutes. Five minutes is the longest SMTO allows for a single Docker action.

What success looks like

  • The containers, images or project show the result you wanted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer; slow Docker work can mean that computer is busy or short on disk space. Don't repeat the action again and again without checking the result each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Docker operation on the selected Gateway exceeded its deadline (60 seconds by default, 300 seconds maximum) at a checkpoint; if any Engine or Compose subrequest had already changed state, that effect is kept as unknown.

What this means

  • The operation's bounded deadline elapsed during a checkpoint, with mutation certainty retained across all Engine or Compose subrequests. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The operation's bounded deadline elapsed during a checkpoint, with mutation certainty retained across all Engine or Compose subrequests.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original phase, known_completed steps and exact object state; increasing a timeout does not reconcile an earlier attempt.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the target with read-only tools (docker.containers, docker.images, docker.compose_ps) and settle what the timed-out operation did. If more work is still needed and the operation is legitimately slow (large pull or build), submit a new request with a larger timeout argument, up to 300 seconds.
  • Inspect the timed-out operation and reconcile possible effects before another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The original outcome is settled before any justified new operation with a suitable supported deadline.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
